picks.what: The East Prospect of Birmingham, engraving
picks.why: the classic general view with St. Martin’s spire and the new St. Philip’s; title and key text cut; low resolution

picks.file: A poetic survey round Birmingham - James Bisset - 1800 - plate Q.jpg
picks.what: View from the Warwick Canal, engraving in James Bisset’s Magnificent Directory
picks.why: true dated view with St. Martin’s and St. Philip’s and smoking factories; trimmed off the directory text; small (about 800 px wide), photographed from the book

picks.file: -Group of 6 Early Stereograph Views of Birmingham, England- MET DP72780.jpg
picks.what: The Town Hall and Christ Church, stereo photograph (Metropolitan Museum of Art)
picks.why: left half of the stereo card; Town Hall with the spire of Christ Church (demolished 1899); the Met dates it 1860s–80s

picks.what: Panorama of the city center skyline, photograph
picks.why: wide, sharp skyline of the city center towers; some sky cut

gaps: P0, P1: nothing; P5: only 1948 RAF aerials of rail yards, suburbs and a golf course, not recognizable
notes: Many hits are other Birminghams: #2 and #10 are Pittsburgh (Birmingham, Pennsylvania), #8, #9, #16–#18 Birmingham, Alabama, #26–#27 Baie-Mahault, Guadeloupe. #23–#24 are photos of a museum gallery. #3 is a generic landscape of the ‘environs’. #6 (J. I. Richards, Old Cross and St. Martin’s) must predate the Cross’s removal in 1784 but has no firmer date than ‘before 1811’, so skipped. #7 (James Holland) is undated; 1799 is the painter’s birth year. #4 is weak (small, page photo) and can be dropped if a better P3 turns up.
